Exit code 1
# Matrix handoff

Prepared by the matrix session (Claude) on 2026-09-25. This file acknowledges `HANDOFF-CODEX.md` and accepts its ownership split. The matrix session writes this file and everything under `matrix/`. It doesn't touch `runs/`, `builds/`, `reviews/` or `HANDOFF-CODEX.md`.

## Candidate

- Branch `push-pull-validation-head` at `b3796a70b526541014c92a40f685389060b862fe`, local only, in `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/push-pull-validation`.
- It is main `4a13294a` plus #1383 (ENG-2131), #1475 (ENG-2202), #1477 (ENG-2288), #1479 (ENG-2296) and #1482 (Obsidian import file names, external). It merged with no conflicts. #1412 was left out because it only adds tests and is based on a pre-merge branch.
- The candidate has no Supabase migrations. Its only `packages/database` change is converter code (`src/lib/crossAppConverters.ts`, +1 line).
- CI receipt: `matrix/receipts/ci-validate-b3796a70.log` records `pnpm ci:validate` passing on `b3796a70`, with 8/8 check-types and all unit suites (roam 62 files, obsidian 6, database 7, content-model 2, website).

## Files

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `matrix/cases.json` | Canonical cases. sha256 `27e594091fbf66f57db56636c0ba6ef92dcb1c0266d6687001d85599e7e1285e` |
| `matrix/push-pull-test-matrix.tsv` | One row per case and direction, in the bug-bash sheet's column order. sha256 `adf470313c555fb53511c462e64d0274e229e54211286eaa0b5b4b53283e97f5` |
| `matrix/push-pull-test-matrix.html` | Generated page. sha256 `e65c42c32019a1a7caab681e941e1af7463bd48068e830fe47634792b38a2ac1` |
| `matrix/template.html`, `matrix/build.mjs`, `matrix/check.mjs` | Generator: `node matrix/build.mjs` rebuilds the page and TSV from `cases.json`; `node matrix/check.mjs` checks the page script parses |
| `matrix/recon/*.md` | The six code-reader reports behind the ratings: roam-source, roam-destination, obsidian, database, linear-specs, github-context |

The published page is private to Sid: https://claude.ai/artifact/PPJhCiaXpp7LB7C11GRpTf. To update it, read that URL with the Artifact tool, then republish the rebuilt HTML with `url` set to it.

## Case schema

Each case in `cases.json` has these fields:

- `id`: stable across revisions.
- `area`: one of JRN, PUB, DSC, TXT, TTL, SRC, AST, UPD, DEL, REL, SCH, CNV, COL, RND, UX, SCL, SEC.
- `title`
- `dirs`: any of RR, RO, OR, OO, 3S (three spaces), DB (database).
- `steps`
- `expected`: the observable outcome, or "Not specified" for a product question.
- `src`: the ticket or document behind `expected`.
- `rating`:
  - `risk`: code reading suggests `expected` won't hold.
  - `decide`: needs a product decision.
  - `gap`: known or accepted for v0.
  - `pass`: expected to pass.
  - `unknown`
- `why`
- `ev`: code or PR references for the rating.
- `method`: `bash` (real-product bug bash), `db` (local database test) or `auto` (automated conversion test).
- `evidence`: what a pass records, `shot` (screenshot), `log` (assertion output or log) or `receipt` (written receipt). Failures always get the failure capture and, later, a video.
- `pri`: P0 to P2.
- `smoke`: set on the four journeys.
- `iso`: needs throwaway spaces.

Counts at this revision:

- 172 cases.
- Ratings: 43 risk, 22 decide, 21 gap, 56 pass, 30 unknown.
- Methods: 156 bash, 10 db, 6 auto.
- Journeys J-RR, J-RO, J-OR and J-OO are the smoke checks.

A rating is a code hypothesis, not a result. A `decide` row stays unresolved until an expected outcome is agreed.

## What the matrix session checked by hand

Everything else in `why` comes from the reader reports and cites code, but wasn't re-read by hand.

- **UPD-04.** `getImportedNodeUids` has no page restriction, so refresh-all also walks relation, schema and type blocks that carry `importedFrom` (`apps/roam/src/utils/importedSourceIdentity.ts:81-94`, `refreshAllImportedNodes.ts:13`).
- **DEL-04.** `loadRelations` returns an empty file on any read, parse or shape error (`apps/obsidian/src/utils/relationsStore.ts:35-62`), and orphan relation deletion then removes every synced relation concept (`apps/obsidian/src/utils/publishNode.ts:296-310`).
- **DEL-05.**
  - Confirmed: at load, `initializeSupabaseSync` runs `cleanupOrphanedNodes` (`apps/obsidian/src/utils/syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:1133-1149`), which builds the local set from `metadataCache.getFileCache(file)?.frontmatter` (`apps/obsidian/src/utils/getDiscourseNodes.ts:18-52`).
  - Not confirmed: whether the cache can be incomplete at that moment.
- **SEC-01 and SEC-02.** See below.
- **SEC-05, partly.** The storage update policy checks only the bucket (`packages/database/supabase/schemas/assets.sql:155-157`).

## Access-control hypotheses

Both are unverified and high priority. Test only on an isolated local database, as an ordinary authenticated outsider with no membership in the target space or group. Keep privileged setup separate from the action under test, and include a permitted-member control. Keep the evidence local and restricted. If confirmed, file a private Linear issue, never a public GitHub issue or attachment.

**SEC-01: outsider grants itself access through the account functions.**
- **Invariant:** a caller with no SpaceAccess on space S cannot create or raise SpaceAccess on S for any account through `upsert_account_in_space`, `upsert_accounts_in_space` or `create_account_in_space`.
- **Where:** `packages/database/supabase/schemas/account.sql`.
  - `my_permissions_in_space` (228-237) returns `max(permissions)` over the caller's accounts, which is NULL for a non-member.
  - `upsert_account_in_space` (324-371) is SECURITY DEFINER with no membership check. It inserts SpaceAccess with `least(my_permissions_in_space(space_id_), COALESCE(permissions_, 'editor'))`. PostgreSQL's `LEAST` ignores NULL, so the value becomes the requested permission, `editor` by default.
  - The wrappers `upsert_accounts_in_space` (373-395) and `create_account_in_space` (397-410) call it.
  - Migration source: `migrations/20260213155959_upsert_user_permissions.sql`.
- **Precondition to confirm:** the grant goes to the `dg_account` of the PlatformAccount matching (`account_local_id`, S's platform). So escalation needs an `account_local_id` on S's platform whose `dg_account` is the caller's own auth uid.
- **What to observe:**
  - the RPC result
  - the SpaceAccess row
  - reads of S's Concept and Content, and writes to S's rows, as the caller afterwards

**SEC-02: outsider joins through a group membership row.**
- **Invariant:** a caller can add a membership only for a group it administers, and `group_id` must be a group account. No insert can make another space's account uid part of the caller's `my_user_accounts()`.
- **Where:** `packages/database/supabase/schemas/account.sql`.
  - Table at 140-147: `admin` defaults to true.
  - `my_user_accounts` at 216-224 returns the caller's uid plus every `group_id` it is a member of.
  - `group_exists` at 257-263 is true only when any membership row has that `group_id`.
  - Insert policy at 586: `is_group_admin(group_id) OR NOT group_exists(group_id)`. There is no check on `member_id` or on the kind of account.
  - Migration source: `migrations/20260101183250_group_access.sql:62`.
- **Variants:**
  - (a) `group_id` is another space's anon uid. Co-member uids are visible through the group_membership select policy (580) and `my_pseudo_accounts` (461-477).
  - (b) Rejoin a group all of whose members have left.
- **What to observe:**
  - whether the insert succeeds
  - the resulting `my_user_accounts()`
  - reads and writes in the target space

**Lower priority, also from the database reader:**
- **SEC-03:** any member of a grantee group can delete that group's ResourceAccess rows (`content.sql:740`). This is a decision, not yet a bug.
- **SEC-04:** after SpaceAccess removal, reads still work through ResourceAccess on the tables and storage (`content.sql:726`, `assets.sql:83-94`).
- **SEC-05:** storage insert and update check only the bucket, and importers don't compare downloaded bytes with the hash (`assets.sql:134-157`).
- **SEC-06:** `create-space` upserts the Space name before checking the password (`packages/database/supabase/functions/create-space/index.ts:77-117`).

## Open decisions for Sid

Cases rated `decide` at P0 or P1:

- SRC-03: placeholder, or keep the incoming title and warn?
- PUB-04 and DEL-03: is there any unshare in v0?
- PUB-11: should publish warn when the Source is synced but not shared?
- DSC-06: what happens when the source space leaves the group?
- TXT-04: may Obsidian links and tags create Roam pages?
- TXT-06: should Refresh keep block ids?
- TTL-11: two nodes with the same title from two spaces
- TTL-15: a node renamed so it no longer matches any format
- AST-06: linked, not embedded, Obsidian files
- AST-08: where assets land in Obsidian
- UPD-09: a sign that a newer version exists
- REL-05: should removed relations stay removed?
- REL-07 and REL-08: when do new relations arrive?
- REL-09: an upstream deletion of a relation that was accepted locally
- SEC-03

## Next for the matrix session

- Take Codex's review of the high-risk rows. Update ratings only with evidence, keep IDs stable, record each revision's hash here, and rebuild.
- Review `runs/templates/*` against the case fields.
- When Sid approves, put the canonical cases into ENG-1881. Per Sid's Linear preference, give him raw markdown to paste.
- Start a fresh session for this, reading this file and `matrix/recon/` rather than relying on the original conversation.

# Independent review of the combined validation matrix

The 172-case matrix has useful breadth, but several steps and expectations need correction before it becomes the execution checklist. All 43 high-risk rows have an independent source review in `codex-high-risk-review.json`. These are code findings, not test results. No live application, database or security check was executed.

The matrix session remains the sole writer of the canonical cases. This report proposes changes for that session to incorporate.

## Reviewed inputs

- Candidate: `push-pull-validation-head`, `b3796a70b526541014c92a40f685389060b862fe`.
- Runtime source was read in Codex's worktree at `09d97321`. Its five-PR runtime merge has exactly the same Git tree as the candidate. The remaining changes are tests, test configuration and the prior inventory.
- Canonical matrix: `/mnt/data/projects/dg-validation-eng-1883/matrix/cases.json`. The scratchpad copy used during review has the same bytes.
- Matrix SHA-256: `27e594091fbf66f57db56636c0ba6ef92dcb1c0266d6687001d85599e7e1285e`.
- Frozen review input: `codex-input-cases-27e59409.json`. It is evidence for this review, not another canonical matrix.
- Verified inventory: 172 unique case IDs, 17 areas, 43 high risk, 22 needs a decision, 21 known gaps, 56 expected to pass and 30 unknown. The TSV contains 376 data rows with 16 columns each, matching the current direction expansion. Generic `3S` rows have not yet been expanded into concrete platform assignments.
- The private artifact URL could not be opened through the available web tool. The local JSON and TSV were read directly. The HTML page and Copy button were not tested.

Source references below are relative to the pinned runtime tree. The per-case JSON includes further references.

## Corrections before execution

1. **J-RR, J-RO, J-OR, J-OO: import the Claim before expecting its relation.** The journeys publish Source, Evidence and Claim, then import only Evidence and expect the Claim relation to be pending. Automatic Source import does not import the unrelated Claim endpoint. Roam discovery filters for both endpoints being local/imported (`apps/roam/src/utils/discoverSharedRelations.ts:88`); Obsidian relation import skips an unresolved endpoint (`apps/obsidian/src/utils/importRelations.ts:263`). First import Evidence and check Source inclusion. Then explicitly import Claim, check the pending relation and accept it. A later refresh of a deleted Claim also requires a Claim copy to exist locally. Wait for observed source sync/cleanup before destination refresh; elapsed time alone is not proof.

2. **SRC-03: the ordinary missing-Source behavior is already settled.** Sid's supplied meeting notes explicitly selected `[[@placeholder]]`. The current candidate implements it in `apps/roam/src/utils/sourceSlot.ts:15` and `apps/roam/src/utils/materializeSharedNode.ts:178`. Test placeholder plus warning for a Source-bearing type and core title. Keep the existing collision fallback as a separate fixture: if the synthesized placeholder title collides, the candidate retains the incoming title and warns (`materializeSharedNode.ts:184`). Older ticket prose does not require reopening the ordinary placeholder choice.

3. **PUB-07: remove the obsolete zero-success message claim.** `apps/roam/src/components/Export.tsx:899` now says `No nodes were published.` when there are no successes. Lines 931 onward use warning intent and leave the dialog open. Mixed-row and schema/relation failure accounting still deserve tests, but the old message is not evidence against this candidate.

4. **UPD-04: allow legitimate skipped nodes.** Refresh-all deliberately skips unchanged content (`apps/roam/src/utils/materializeSharedNode.ts:431`). The assertion should be no spurious failures and correct node-only totals. The broad import-marker query still supports the concern that schema pages and relation blocks enter the batch (`apps/roam/src/utils/importedSourceIdentity.ts:81`).

5. **SRC-04: distinguish remote availability from a local Source copy.** A forced refresh resolves a Source already present in the destination; it does not import a newly published Source (`apps/roam/src/utils/materializeSharedNode.ts:145`). To isolate the unchanged-timestamp problem, publish the Source, explicitly import it locally, then compare refresh-all with forced refresh on the unchanged Evidence. Keep automatic dependency import as a separate initial-import check.

6. **SRC-06, UPD-10 and UPD-11: avoid reloads while testing the failure cutoff.** The counter is module state and retries use exponential backoff (`apps/roam/src/utils/syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:894`, `:1674`). Five reloads are not five consecutive failures in one loaded client. Use controlled failure injection/scheduler checks or observe the same loaded client. Distinguish error messages during a failed run from a message that future scheduling stopped. Roam's normal scheduling baseline is five minutes; Obsidian's edit debounce is five seconds. Neither is a completion guarantee.

7. **REL-15: correct the identifier explanation.** The visibility concern has source support, but the stored endpoint is a constructed RID, while `getRelationsForFile` looks for the bare local node ID or imported RID (`apps/obsidian/src/utils/relationsStore.ts:246`, `:441`). An original local note normally has no imported RID. Check both endpoint panels and the stored relation independently.

8. **UX-03 and UX-07: make the triggers sufficient.** UX-03 needs a relation-stage exception in addition to all selected node imports failing; missing endpoints can simply filter the relations out. UX-07 needs an uncached source name; restarting alone is insufficient because names are saved in settings (`apps/obsidian/src/components/ImportNodesModal.tsx:86`).

9. **DSC-10 and UX-06: distinguish error details from aggregate results.** Obsidian increments failed node counts when required type metadata is absent, and its modal reports that count. Calling the whole path console-only is inaccurate. Automatic Source imports are not included in the selected-root success count; decide whether that notice counts selections or every implicit write before treating the count as wrong. Missing asset feedback is a separate assertion.

10. **TXT-08: recheck its obsolete heading-removal premise.** The current Roam importer strips Obsidian frontmatter and trims blank lines, then passes the body through (`apps/roam/src/utils/materializeSharedNode.ts:223`). This path does not contain the claimed leading-title-heading removal. Keep a real first-heading fixture, but do not turn an old implementation detail into an unresolved product decision without fresh evidence.

## Findings to test early

Source supports the alternate Roam publication paths in PUB-05, native Roam media-macro rewriting concern in AST-04, overly broad refresh enumeration in UPD-04, and the unreadable relation-store path in DEL-04. None has been reproduced live in this review.

For DEL-04, seed known relation IDs, induce a read or parse failure, let the remaining full-sync stages complete, and inspect database state. An empty fallback reaches orphan deletion in `apps/obsidian/src/utils/publishNode.ts:296`. Do not use an unchanged accepted relation at a destination as the only evidence: destination deletion reconciliation is itself unresolved. The deletion is bounded by the IDs fetched, so the claim that every relation is deleted needs qualification for stores exceeding the API row limit.

For REL-13/14/15 and RND-02, observe publication, persistence, discovery, materialization and both endpoint views separately. A producer failure must not be misclassified as a consumer failure. For Obsidian, also check after the next full sync, which reconciles relation grants.

The security rows remain local-test hypotheses. SEC-01/02 have independently inspected SQL paths, including corresponding migrations. SEC-05 should separate overwriting a readable object from pre-seeding a new key; effective SELECT/Storage API rules matter. SEC-06 needs the local edge function and a persisted-state check. SEC-04 needs an explicit policy expectation for how SpaceAccess removal affects independent ResourceAccess grants. Removing a resource grant is a distinct control. Keep detailed execution evidence restricted and do not test these against the deployed service.

## Coverage additions and execution details

- **Add a source-space identity collision case for Obsidian discovery.** Publish distinct nodes from two spaces with the same `source_local_id`/`nodeInstanceId`. Import one and check the other remains discoverable, then check a collision with a destination-owned node. The modal filters using the bare ID (`apps/obsidian/src/components/ImportNodesModal.tsx:74`) collected without space identity (`apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts:92`). Different titles do not prevent this collision. This is separate from the existing same-title cases.
- **Expand three-space assignments.** Name A as original owner, B as contributor and C as third consumer. Use RRR, RRO, ROR, ROO, ORR, ORO, OOR and OOO where applicable. REL-13 has B=R; REL-14 has B=O. REL-15 and RND-02 overlap on A importing B's contribution, so map that coverage rather than counting the same execution twice. Record account/group membership independently of platform letters.
- **Extend COL-01/02 with stable authorship assertions.** Use named creator U1 and editor/publisher U2. Check source creator IDs on node/schema/content records before and after ordinary sync, explicit publish and asset retry. A display name alone cannot prove author identity stayed correct. This covers the database boundary left open by schema metadata unit tests.
- **Keep ratings separate from result status.** The input JSON encodes expected-to-pass as `rating: "pass"`. It means a prediction, not an executed pass. Run receipts must start as not run and pin the matrix hash.
- **Use the app/API boundary for pagination tests.** Direct SQL counts cannot demonstrate the PostgREST truncation in SCL-03/04. Record effective `max_rows` and ensure the omitted/deleted ID is outside the observed result page.

## Execution and publication state

The other session has put its canonical JSON/TSV/page and `HANDOFF-MATRIX.md` into the agreed shared folder. Their case hash matches the reviewed input. That session should now incorporate or respond to this review. Codex has not edited its scratchpad or canonical cases.

Sid selected isolated local Supabase for run 1. The later team bug bash uses the deployed backend with throwaway spaces and a test group, and excludes all `iso` and `SEC` cases. Local-database-method cases also stay local. Existing `09d97321` bundles target the deployed backend and retain that provenance; they are not the local run artifacts. Fresh artifacts and effective local endpoints remain to be prepared.

Pushing the candidate, sharing the private artifact and updating Linear have not been authorized or performed by this review. Once publishing is authorized, ENG-1881 should remain the matrix owner's write and ENG-1883 the run owner's write. Preserve the ticket's acceptance scope; attach or link the versioned matrix instead of replacing the ticket with hundreds of execution rows unless Sid explicitly prefers that format.

`HANDOFF-MATRIX.md` says every failure gets a later video. Keep the agreed selection step: every observed failure gets a capture, while a separate recording is useful when it explains the failure or a product decision. Existing reproducible assertion/log evidence does not automatically require another video.

Review: **supported path**

Retain all four A/B platform assignments. Capture B publication separately from A materialization so REL-13/14 producer failure does not masquerade as REL-15 consumer failure.

Source: `apps/roam/src/utils/roamToCrossAppConverters.ts:155`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/publishNode.ts:101`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/relationsStore.ts:246`.

## UX-02

Review: **supported path**

Node results are set before the relation await, but progress is cleared only in finally and controls remain disabled while importing. Observe the intermediate state with a controlled delayed relation stage.

Source: `apps/roam/src/components/DiscoverSharedNodesDialog.tsx:321`, `apps/roam/src/components/DiscoverSharedNodesDialog.tsx:339`, `apps/roam/src/components/DiscoverSharedNodesDialog.tsx:407`.

## UX-03

Review: **revise steps**

The misleading message exists only when the relation stage throws. All selected nodes failing does not itself make that stage throw, especially when no endpoints resolve. Add an explicit eligible relation-stage failure and distinguish it from the node failures.

Source: `apps/roam/src/components/DiscoverSharedNodesDialog.tsx:339`, `apps/roam/src/utils/discoverSharedRelations.ts:88`.

## UX-06

Review: **qualify oracle**

Recursive Source import results are not added to the selected-root success count, and asset errors are separate from node failure counts. Agree whether the notice counts selections or every implicit node before declaring its count wrong; assert missing asset feedback separately.

Source: `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts:1459`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts:1785`, `apps/obsidian/src/components/ImportNodesModal.tsx:225`.

## UX-07

Review: **revise steps**

Space names are saved in plugin settings, so restart alone does not clear them. Use a genuinely uncached source or controlled removal of the test cache entry. The fallback naming path is present.

Source: `apps/obsidian/src/components/ImportNodesModal.tsx:86`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/typeUtils.ts:48`.

## SCL-03

Review: **supported path**

The getters do not paginate and local API max_rows is 1000. Exercise the actual PostgREST/app getters; a direct SQL row count bypasses the suspected truncation. Record the effective target configuration.

Source: `packages/database/src/lib/sharedNodes.ts:294`, `packages/database/supabase/config.toml:18`.

## SCL-04

Review: **supported path**

Cleanup scans also lack pagination. Establish that the deleted ID lies outside the returned page instead of relying on unspecified row ordering. Obsidian content variants can exhaust the limit with fewer distinct nodes.

Source: `apps/roam/src/utils/cleanupOrphanedNodes.ts:12`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts:67`.

## SEC-01

Review: **local test needed**

The definer function has no explicit membership guard before its grant insertion; the same path exists in migrations. Verify effective execute privileges and an ordinary authenticated account whose platform identity is linked. No DB call has been made.

Source: `packages/database/supabase/schemas/account.sql:324`, `packages/database/supabase/migrations/20260213155959_upsert_user_permissions.sql:12`.

## SEC-02

Review: **local test needed**

Group bootstrap permits insertion when no membership rows exist, and account access derives from those group IDs. Check effective policies, constraints and legitimate group-creation controls on an isolated migrated database. No DB call has been made.

Source: `packages/database/supabase/schemas/account.sql:216`, `packages/database/supabase/schemas/account.sql:257`, `packages/database/supabase/schemas/account.sql:586`, `packages/database/supabase/migrations/20260101183250_group_access.sql:62`.

## SEC-04

Review: **policy oracle needed**

Per-resource grants can independently authorize table/storage access after SpaceAccess removal. Characterize the difference, but settle whether removing SpaceAccess revokes existing ResourceAccess grants before calling this unauthorized. Include explicit resource-grant revocation as a control.

Source: `packages/database/supabase/schemas/content.sql:203`, `packages/database/supabase/schemas/content.sql:726`, `packages/database/supabase/schemas/assets.sql:83`.

## SEC-05

Review: **qualify trigger**

The broad asset write policies merit local testing. Existing-object overwrite must account for SELECT policy and Storage API requirements; test an authorized reader without write authority separately from pre-seeding a fresh object key. Obsidian hashes existing local files for collision handling, which is different from verifying newly downloaded bytes.

Source: `packages/database/supabase/schemas/assets.sql:134`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts:793`, `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts:1067`.

## SEC-06

Review: **local test needed**

The edge function uses a privileged client and upserts the space before validating its password. Test the local edge endpoint and persisted state on an existing synthetic space; a returned authentication error alone is not sufficient evidence.

Source: `packages/database/supabase/functions/create-space/index.ts:77`, `packages/database/supabase/functions/create-space/index.ts:101`, `packages/database/supabase/functions/create-space/index.ts:263`.

"""Edit cases.json in place, re-serializing only the cases that change.

Unchanged cases keep their exact bytes. Changed and new cases use the file's
six-line layout. Run with the edits module path as argv[1].
"""

import hashlib
import importlib.util
import json
import sys

PATH = "/mnt/data/projects/dg-validation-eng-1883/matrix/cases.json"
ORDER = ["id", "area", "smoke", "title", "dirs", "steps", "expected", "src",
         "rating", "why", "ev", "method", "evidence", "pri", "iso"]


def j(v):
    return json.dumps(v, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))


def serialize(c):
    unknown = set(c) - set(ORDER)
    assert not unknown, unknown
    head = [f'"id":{j(c["id"])}', f'"area":{j(c["area"])}']
    if c.get("smoke"):
        head.append('"smoke":true')
    head += [f'"title":{j(c["title"])}', f'"dirs":{j(c["dirs"])}']
    tail = [f'"ev":{j(c["ev"])}', f'"method":{j(c["method"])}',
            f'"evidence":{j(c["evidence"])}', f'"pri":{j(c["pri"])}']
    if c.get("iso"):
        tail.append('"iso":true')
    return (
        "{" + ",".join(head) + ",\n"
        f' "steps":{j(c["steps"])},\n'
        f' "expected":{j(c["expected"])},\n'
        f' "src":{j(c["src"])},"rating":{j(c["rating"])},\n'
        f' "why":{j(c["why"])},\n'
        " " + ",".join(tail) + "}"
    )


def spans(text):
    dec = json.JSONDecoder()
    out = {}
    i = text.index("[") + 1
    while True:
        k = text.find('{"id":', i)
        if k < 0:
            break
        obj, end = dec.raw_decode(text, k)
        out[obj["id"]] = (k, end, obj)
        i = end
    return out


def main():
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("edits", sys.argv[1])
    edits = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(edits)

    text = open(PATH, encoding="utf8").read()
    before = hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest()
    sp = spans(text)

    # Changes: id -> dict of field updates (None deletes the field).
    repl = []
    for cid, upd in edits.CHANGES.items():
        k, end, obj = sp[cid]
        new = dict(obj)
        for f, v in upd.items():
            if v is None:
                new.pop(f, None)
            else:
                new[f] = v
        assert new["id"] == cid
        repl.append((k, end, serialize(new)))

    # Additions: list of (after_id, case)
    for after, case in edits.ADDITIONS:
        assert case["id"] not in sp, case["id"]
        k, end, _ = sp[after]
        repl.append((end, end, ",\n" + serialize(case)))

    repl.sort(key=lambda r: (r[0], r[1]))
    out, pos = [], 0
    for k, end, s in repl:
        assert k >= pos, "overlapping edits"
        out.append(text[pos:k])
        out.append(s)
        pos = end
    out.append(text[pos:])
    result = "".join(out)

    data = json.loads(result)
    ids = [c["id"] for c in data]
    assert len(ids) == len(set(ids)), "duplicate ids"
    orig_ids = [c["id"] for c in json.loads(text)]
    assert all(i in ids for i in orig_ids), "lost an id"
    for c in data:
        for f in ["id", "area", "title", "dirs", "steps", "expected", "src",
                  "rating", "why", "ev", "method", "evidence", "pri"]:
            assert f in c, (c["id"], f)
        assert c["rating"] in {"risk", "decide", "gap", "pass", "unknown"}, c["id"]
        assert c["method"] in {"bash", "db", "auto"}, c["id"]
        assert c["evidence"] in {"shot", "log", "receipt"}, c["id"]
        assert c["pri"] in {"P0", "P1", "P2"}, c["id"]
    open(PATH, "w", encoding="utf8").write(result)
    after = hashlib.sha256(result.encode()).hexdigest()
    print(f"before={before}\nafter={after}\ncases={len(data)} changed={len(edits.CHANGES)} added={len(edits.ADDITIONS)}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# DG Engineering Writing Style

Write in a direct, concise, plainspoken style that preserves important context and qualification.

## Core style

- Lead with the relevant point and move quickly to the concrete question, request, or action.
- Prefer the shortest version that remains clear and preserves necessary nuance.
- Identify wording or missing context that is ambiguous or could be misconstrued. Resolve it when the intended meaning is clear; otherwise, flag it and ask for clarification.
- Use natural contractions and everyday wording. Avoid corporate jargon, inflated phrasing, and generic professional filler.
- Avoid em dashes as sentence-level punctuation. Use a period, comma, colon, semicolon, or parentheses to separate thoughts instead. Preserve em dashes only when they appear in exact quotations, titles, source text, or technical content supplied by the requester.
- When identifying a problem or disagreement, state it plainly and pivot toward clarification, resolution, criteria, or next steps.
- Prefer bullets for distinct points. When prose reads more naturally, keep paragraphs and sentences short; avoid run-on sentences.
- Ask one clear question when one will do. Combine related questions only when separating them would add needless length.

## Adapt to the channel

- For a quick reply or chat message, omit the greeting and sign-off when they add no value.
- For technical issues, describe the observed behavior, the relevant contrast or expectation, and the requested clarification or next step.
- For engineering tickets and technical documentation, apply these ASD-STE100-inspired principles:
  - Use one term consistently for each concept. Do not alternate between synonyms.
  - Put one primary action or idea in each sentence.
  - Prefer active voice when the actor is important.
  - Replace vague verbs such as "handle," "support," or "improve" with the specific behavior or result.

## Drafting rules

- Preserve facts, commitments, dates, names, links, and technical meaning supplied by the requester.
- Do not invent availability, decisions, commitments, or emotional language.
- Treat explicit directions such as "shorter," "warmer," "more forceful," "broader," or "one sentence" as overrides for the current draft.
- When the requester asks for alternatives, vary the framing or emphasis rather than making superficial synonym swaps.
- Return a ready-to-use draft first. Add explanation only when requested or when an ambiguity materially affects the wording.

content.text:
## Page contract — read before your first publish

These are the Artifact tool's own rules for the file you publish; the design guidance below builds on them.

**Format**: Always author the page as `.html`. Publish a `.md` file only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it. When the user shares a markdown document or asks to turn one into an artifact, author an HTML page based on its content — preserve its substance, and design the page as you would any other artifact rather than transcribing the markdown one-to-one.

**Skeleton**: The file is wrapped in a `<!doctype html>…<head>…</head><body>` skeleton at publish time, so write the page content directly — no `<!DOCTYPE>`, `<html>`, `<head>`, or `<body>` tags of your own. Its head carries only a charset and viewport meta (with `viewport-fit=cover`) plus a small reset — light `color-scheme`, `:root` padded top and bottom by the phone's safe-area insets, zero body margin with a 14px system font on an off-white ground, `img{max-width:100%}`, and `[hidden]{display:none!important}` (toggle visibility with `el.hidden`, not `style.display`) — so put your own `<title>` and `<style>` at the top of the file. Keep the `:root` padding: a bar fixed to the top or bottom stays at `0` and adds `env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)` or `env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)` to its own padding, and a sticky page header uses `top: env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)`, not `0`.

**Title**: Set a `<title>` at the top of the HTML — only the first 8KB of the file is scanned for it. It names the artifact in the browser tab and gallery, so make it a name, not a summary: a short noun phrase, typically two to four words, distinctive to this page's subject so the reader can pick it out of a gallery of many — the way an app or a document gets named, never a generic category label, and never a name plus an appended explainer after a dash or colon. When a natural title pairs the name with a generic word, the name is the half that survives the trim — keeping the generic half and dropping the identity makes the title worse, not shorter. And trim only actual explainers: a multi-word title that already reads as one specific name is finished as it is. The explanation belongs in the `description` parameter instead: pass a one-sentence `description` — it becomes the gallery card's subtitle. For HTML publishes, a `title` parameter fills in when the file has no tag (Markdown pages always keep their filename identity). Keep the title stable across redeploys.

**External resources — CDN allowlist (CSP-enforced)**: external scripts load ONLY from https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com (preferred), https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/, https://unpkg.com, https://cdn.tailwindcss.com (Tailwind's play-CDN script) and https://code.jquery.com; external stylesheets ONLY from https://fonts.googleapis.com, with the font files they pull from https://fonts.gstatic.com (give every face a real fallback stack). Everything else is blocked, with no visible error: every other host (esm.sh included) and, even on those CDNs, anything but a script — stylesheets, images, media, fetch/XHR/WebSocket, a library's runtime fetches. So inline all other CSS and JS and embed assets as data: URIs. **How to load a library**: `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/<lib>/<exact version>/<file>">` — pick the UMD build, which defines a global (e.g. react/18.3.1/umd/react.production.min.js, then react-dom) — placed BEFORE any inline `<script>` that uses it; always pin an exact version. The viewer's sandbox also blocks any download the page starts itself — `<a download>` links (data:/blob: hrefs included) and script-driven saves are inert for viewers — so never offer a file through a plain link. Links to other websites (`https://…`) open in a new tab, but email, phone and app links (`mailto:`, `tel:`, `sms:`, other custom schemes) are unreliable inside an artifact: for many viewers (for example anyone outside the user's organization, or anyone viewing through a public link) following one, by link or by script, often does not work, and the page cannot tell whether it did. So show the address or number itself as selectable text (a copy button helps), treat such a link as a convenience that may do nothing, and never tell the viewer a message was sent or a call placed because the viewer tapped one. Artifacts render mermaid diagrams natively — markdown via ```mermaid fences, HTML via `<pre class="mermaid">` blocks — no library needed, don't load one. The viewer never shows `alert()`, `confirm()` or `prompt()` dialogs — `confirm()` returns false and `prompt()` returns null immediately — so build any confirmation step into the page itself.

**What the viewer's frame allows**: The page runs in a locked-down frame; what it refuses below, it refuses for every viewer (anonymous, signed-in, embedded, desktop and mobile apps), so build around these limits instead of detecting them. The page cannot open the print dialog — `window.print()` does nothing — so never offer a Print or "Save as PDF" button. Forms work as page UI (inputs, validation, submit events), but a real submission has nowhere to go: handle `submit` in script with `preventDefault()` and never point `action` at another site or a mailto: address. Copy buttons work when `navigator.clipboard.writeText` is called inside the click handler — catch its rejection (older desktop apps and some app views refuse it) and fall back to selecting the text; reading the clipboard never works, though the viewer's own Paste (the `paste` event) does. Camera, microphone, screen capture, location, Web Share and similar device APIs are refused without a prompt — don't build features on them (a screen wake lock may be granted while the page is visible: request it and tolerate rejection); file inputs, drag-and-drop of files and `FileReader` work in browsers, so take photos, audio and data as uploaded files instead. Fullscreen and pointer lock work from a click in desktop browsers; treat both as optional (handle the rejection) since phones and some app views lack them. Sound plays only after the viewer interacts (muted autoplay is fine), so start audio from a button. Other sites cannot be embedded — no YouTube, map or form iframes, and no `<object>`/`<embed>`; link out instead: links open outside the artifact, normally in a new tab, while `window.open` works only for some signed-in viewers in the artifact's own organization and returns null for everyone else, so use real `<a href>` links. Web Workers work from your own files or `blob:` URLs; service workers and WebRTC do not. `fetch()` of files published alongside the page works with relative URLs; images from your own files, `data:` or `blob:` URLs draw to canvas and export cleanly. Only a plain `#anchor` (letters, digits, `.` `_` `~` `-`) from the artifact's link reaches `location.hash` — never `#key=value` state and never the query string — so deep-link to a tab or section with a bare token and keep all other state in the page.

**Browser storage**: `localStorage` (also `sessionStorage` and IndexedDB) works, but each artifact has its own origin and the data lives only in that viewer's browser — it survives republishes to the same URL and never reaches other viewers, other devices, or Claude. It can come back empty or the accessor can throw (a private window, cleared or blocked site data, previews or thumbnail capture), so wrap every read and write in try/catch and render the page correctly without it. Use it only for per-viewer conveniences (a remembered tab or filter, a collapsed section, an unsent draft), never for state that must persist reliably, be shared between viewers, or be read back by Claude — state like that belongs in a runtime capability when this user has one: load the `artifact-capabilities` skill before writing the page.

**Size**: The rendered page must be 16MB or smaller, and embedded data: URIs count toward that.

**Responsive**: The page must also work at phone width (~400px). Keep a side gutter of at least 16px at every width: set it once as side padding on `body` or one outer wrapper, and give that element any vertical padding with `padding-block`, never a `padding` shorthand that zeroes the sides. Use relative units; let flex/grid rows wrap or stack to one column when narrow; put `max-width:100%` on images and on any `aspect-ratio` box, and no `min-width` wider than the screen on anything. Only tables, diagrams and code blocks may be wider, each inside its own `overflow-x: auto` container — the page body must never scroll horizontally.

**Theme-aware**: Pages render in the viewer's theme, which has three states: an explicit choice stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, and the default "system" setting stamps nothing — only `prefers-color-scheme` separates light from dark. Define the complete light palette as tokens on bare `:root` (dark-first designs swap the roles consistently); redefine only the tokens under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`, guarded as `:root:not([data-theme="light"])`; redefine them again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]` so the toggle wins in both directions, and set `color-scheme: dark` wherever the dark palette applies — both dark blocks, or bare `:root` in a dark-first or single-dark design (the skeleton pins `light` on `:root`) — so form controls and scrollbars follow. Never give a color its only definition inside a media or `[data-theme]` block, and give `body` an explicit token background — the viewer paints its own ground behind the page, so a transparent body borrows the host's theme. A design that deliberately commits to a single look may skip the dark blocks but still paints background and colors explicitly.

**Icon** (on every first publish): Pass one short generic word as `icon` (e.g. `"chart"`, `"calendar"`, `"recipe"`) for the artifact's browser-tab icon — a plain signifier for what the page is, never a product or brand name, and never an emoji or markup. It stays the **same** for the life of an artifact, so on a redeploy (the same file path this session, or `url`) omit `icon` and the artifact keeps the one it has; pass a different one only when the user asks.

Work the way the design lead at a small, versatile studio would: give each client a visual identity at the level of treatment the task calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Decide the treatment; designing is a given. A doc gets the same craft as a landing page; only the treatment differs. Format is a separate matter: author HTML, and publish Markdown only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it. A Markdown publish keeps its filename as its title, uses almost none of the craft below, and is never a way to save time.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished, with real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages don't need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

If unsure: a well-composed page is always acceptable; an over-designed visual identity sometimes isn't.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. Follow the editorial process after them only when that reading calls for it.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Respect what already exists.** Look for an existing design system first: CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, define it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. Distinctive choices come from the subject's own world: its materials, instruments, and vernacular. Whatever the treatment, include at least one detail only this subject would have (its real units and scales, its document conventions, its terms of art) as content rather than ornament; it costs nothing even on a plain page. Use real content throughout and never lorem ipsum.

**Pair typefaces.** Typography determines how the page reads even when the page isn't about typography. Google Fonts is the only font host the Artifact CSP allows; link it directly (`<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=...&display=swap">`). A face from anywhere else must be inlined as a @font-face data URI, or the browser silently uses a fallback. In both cases, declare a real fallback stack. Keep running text near 65 characters wide. Set a type scale and keep to it. Give headings `text-wrap: balance`, give body text comfortable spacing, and give uppercase labels a little letter-spacing.

**Load libraries instead of inlining them.** When the page really needs a library (React, a charting or highlighting package), load its UMD build from cdnjs with one pinned `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...">` placed before the inline script that uses its global; don't inline the library's source or hand-write a substitute. Only the script loads this way; a library's stylesheet still has to be inlined, and the page contract above lists the few other script hosts the CSP admits. The page's own CSS and JS, its images, and its data ship with the page. Most pages don't need any library; use one only when it does substantial work for the page.

**Choose neutrals deliberately.** A pure mid-grey looks unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent looks intentional. Pure white and near-black are fine backgrounds when they suit the subject, as long as you chose the neutral deliberately instead of inheriting a default.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme, and the viewer has three states: an explicit choice sets `data-theme="dark"` or `data-theme="light"` on the root element, and the default "system" setting sets *nothing*. Most viewers see the document with no `data-theme` attribute, where only `prefers-color-scheme` distinguishes light from dark. Structure the CSS at the token level for all three. The bare `:root` block defines the complete light palette (for a deliberately dark-first design, swap light and dark consistently through this whole pattern); `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` redefines only the tokens, guarded as `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` so an explicit light choice overrides a dark OS setting; `:root[data-theme="dark"]` redefines them again so the toggle also overrides in the other direction; wherever the dark palette applies - both dark blocks, or bare `:root` in a dark-first or single-dark design - also set `color-scheme: dark` (the skeleton pins `light` on `:root`), so native form controls and scrollbars follow the palette. Style components through the tokens, never directly inside a media or `[data-theme]` block: a color defined only inside `[data-theme]` never applies when no `data-theme` attribute is set, and the page then shows one theme's text on the other theme's background. Two more rules keep each theme consistent. First, the artifact is composited over a background the viewer paints in *its own* theme, so `body` must set an explicit `background` from a token; a transparent body shows the host's background with no warning. Second, every element that sets a color takes it from the same token set as the surface behind it, never from a literal that works in only one theme. Declare every token in the bare `:root` block before any media or `[data-theme]` block redefines it; a color that exists only inside one of those blocks is the classic unreadable-artifact bug. Give the second theme the same care as the first: don't simply invert it; keep contrast legible and keep the accent working on both backgrounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme: then omit the media query and `[data-theme]` blocks entirely but still set the background and every color explicitly, so the page looks right on either host background; do this by choice, never by omission.

**Use layout for spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap` instead of per-element margins, which collapse or double without warning. Keep a side gutter of at least 16px at every width: set it once as side padding on `body` or one outer wrapper, whose vertical padding uses `padding-block` and never a `padding` shorthand that zeroes the sides. Let rows wrap or stack to one column at phone width (about 400px). Give images and any `aspect-ratio` box `max-width: 100%`, and don't give anything a `min-width` wider than the screen. Only wide tables, code, and diagrams may exceed it; give each `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. The publish skeleton pads `:root` top and bottom by the phone's safe-area insets (zero everywhere except a phone app) so the page runs edge to edge while its content stays clear of the system bars; keep that padding. A bar fixed to the top or bottom stays at `0` and adds `env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)` or `env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)` to its own padding. A sticky page header uses `top: env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)` and never `0`. Size a one-screen app with `height: 100%` on `html` and `body` instead of `100vh`, so it fits inside that padding. A page that includes its own viewport meta gets this padding only when that meta declares `viewport-fit=cover`. Use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Make repeated elements consistent.** For cards in a row, label/value pairs down a list, or badges on sibling items, use the same edges, baselines, and inner padding on each, and put any recurring element in the same place on each. Let content set a container's height and pick a column count the items fill, so nothing stretches over empty space or sits alone in a row. Make text that can outgrow its track wrap or scroll in its own container; clipped text is a bug.

**Use card styling selectively.** Border, fill, radius, and shadow each mark an element as a separate object. Apply them by role, to set off the one element that needs it; applying the same radius and shadow to every block flattens the hierarchy. Open with big-number tiles only when those figures are the point of the page.

**Draw charts to scale.** Place marks, ticks, and labels with one scale, and make every label name a value the chart actually reaches. Color chart text from the theme tokens so it is readable in both themes. Keep marks, labels, and edges clear of one another and inside the drawing's bounds; in SVG, leave room in the viewBox for the outermost labels and give every drawn shape an explicit fill.

**Make the page complete at rest.** Everything meant to be read is visible once the page has loaded, with no scrolling to trigger it; that first still frame is what a thumbnail, a shared link, and a skimming reader all see. A section may animate in, but from a visible resting state, never left at `opacity: 0` waiting for an observer. Size a hero to its content instead of to the viewport; a `100vh` opener pushes the rest of the page out of that first frame. A tool or app opens in a realistic working state: the user's real data where it exists, otherwise example rows, a loaded sample, or a plausibly filled form, clearly marked as examples and never presented as the user's own figures. The first view shows what the tool does; an empty shell waiting for input shows nothing.

**Avoid AI-generated design.** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. When the user specifies a visual direction, follow it exactly; their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. When nothing is specified, don't use that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly.** Watch for overlapping elements, cascade collisions, and silent font fallbacks. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, and respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. Give every form control a stable `id` (the platform preserves form values, focus, and scroll position across a republish). For generative or decorative graphics, use Canvas or WebGL instead of hand-writing long SVG path data.

**CSS rules.** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificity. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out, e.g. a type-based selector like `.section` and an element-based one like `.cta` both setting padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't undo your spacing unnoticed.

**Writing the copy.** Treat words as design material and never as decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen: name things by what people recognize instead of how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*; they don't manage *webhook config*). Use active voice; a control states exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it, without apologies or vagueness. Prefer specific to clever. Write plainly, the way a knowledgeable person would talk. Avoid mannered devices: asides set off by em-dashes, "not X, but Y" framing, colon-then-reveal sentences, scare quotes around invented labels, and stock phrases such as "worth noting" or "honest caveat". Prefer short, direct sentences over compressed or clever phrasing.

**Name the page like a product; don't caption it.** The `<title>` is the artifact's name in the gallery and the browser tab, and it gives the reader a first impression of the care taken. Give the page a real name: a short noun phrase, typically two to four words, specific to the subject; or, for a page that exists to answer one question, that question itself, which then is the page's name. Stop at the name; a title that adds its own explanation after a dash or colon reads as generated filler. The name must also identify the page among many: in the gallery it appears beside dozens of other artifacts, and a generic category label that could apply to any of them fails as a name just as an appended explanation does. When a candidate title combines the name with a generic word (a greeting, a category, a page-type label), keep the name; a trim that drops the identifying part and keeps the generic word produces a title that could apply to any page. This rule removes explanations and doesn't require brevity: a multi-word title that already reads as one specific name is finished, and shortening it further only makes it generic. Put the explanation in the one-sentence publish `description`; the gallery shows it directly under the title.

**Structure is information.** Structural devices (numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels) should encode something true about the content instead of decorating it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but those fit only if the content actually is a sequence, such as a real process or a typed timeline where the order is information the reader needs. Before adding numbered markers or similar devices, check that they actually make sense.

**When the page is a UI (dashboard, tool).** It is scanned and operated instead of read top to bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Put the summary before the detail. Encode state in form as well as in numbers (a pill, a chip, a severity stripe) so that whatever needs attention is visible at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. Interactive elements should look interactive.



## Process

Start from what the viewer should be able to do on the page, in addition to what they will read. If the page should take input, keep what people change for whoever opens it next, show live data, or ask Claude something, load the `artifact-capabilities` skill now and design around what it makes available to this user. A page that is only read doesn't need that.

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan (a compact token system with color, type, and layout):
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4-6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles: a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

**Write, look once, publish.** Before publishing you may look at the rendered page once: one screenshot of the local file, or the `ArtifactCheck` tool's preview (or the Artifact tool's own `action: "preview"` where there is no separate `ArtifactCheck` tool) where this session offers it. Then make one pass of edits for what it shows, without a second look. For a page that charts real numbers, do take that look instead of skipping it, and use it on the chart. Don't build a test loop around your own file: no repeated screenshots, no pulling the script out to run it through node, no scripts that probe the DOM. Such a loop spends the session re-checking what a careful write already got right, while the user waits for a link. Then publish. A page whose point is logic or stored data takes its one check here, not in a render loop: exercise once any `window.claude` call that the preview couldn't run (read the stored data back, for example), and stop. Review happens on the live page, and further polish is for the user to request. That check is for runtime code you wrote into this page, not for content you fill into an Artifact made from an Artifact type (a Slides deck, a Design canvas): there the type's own instructions say whether to check, and if they say nothing, don't. If the user reports something visibly broken (a clipped column, unreadable text, a control that does nothing), fix that and republish once.

**Open viewers.** You don't need to do anything for viewers who already have the page open: published changes are delivered to them automatically at their next quiet moment, with state preserved where possible. If your page has state a viewer would miss (a game, a long form), register `window.claude?.hot?.snapshot(...)` and boot through `window.claude?.hot?.ready ? window.claude.hot.ready(start) : start(window.claude?.hot?.data ?? {})`.

## When the request is editorial

The stance changes here: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated decisions, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Write the code only after confirming the plan is unique, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero states the thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world (headline, image, live demo, interactive moment). 
- Typography sets the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, avoiding the families you would use on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design instead of a neutral container for the content. 
- Use motion deliberately. Think about whether and where animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. One orchestrated moment is usually more effective than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation adds to the impression that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Put your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent clashes with the background, shift it toward an analogous hue or desaturate it instead of replacing it.
The existing page already meets the contract (title, theme tokens, dark mode, explicit body background), and my changes stay inside it. Trimming the SEC-02 hint, then rebuilding.

input.content:
# Open decisions for ENG-1881

Matrix revision `c601d6efba497946444fe2f9948279e035cbab3651b1371bf0754adcb03d3bdc`, candidate `b3796a70`. These are the "decide" cases at P0 and P1 that Codex's review didn't settle. Each needs an agreed expected result before its case can pass or fail. "Code today" was re-read at `b3796a70`; file references are in the case rows.

The recommended defaults are proposals, not decisions. Where a default needs a code change, the change is named so the case's expected result can be written against it.

## PUB-04 and DEL-03: Is there any way to stop sharing a node in v0?

- **Options**
  - (a) No unshare in v0. Mark it a known gap. Roam shows already-shared groups as checked and locked, as Obsidian does, so the dialog doesn't suggest an action that doesn't exist.
  - (b) Unchecking an already-shared group removes that group's grant for the node on publish.
  - (c) A separate "Stop sharing" action per node and group.
- **Code today**
  - Roam pre-checks a group only when every selected node is shared with it. Unchecking just leaves the group out of this publish, because publish only adds grants.
  - Obsidian shows shared groups with a ✓ and ignores choosing them.
  - Neither app can remove a node's grant. Deleting the node does remove its grants (cleanup, then a database trigger). Leaving the group doesn't, and neither does renaming a Roam node out of its format (TTL-15).
- **Recommended default:** (a). Revoking a grant also raises what happens to relations and to copies already imported (REL-09), which is too much for v0. Deleting the node is the documented way to stop sharing. Expected result for PUB-04: an already-shared group is checked and can't be unchecked.

## PUB-11: Should publish warn when the target group can't see the Evidence's Source?

- **Options**
  - (a) Warn whenever any target group can't see the Source, naming the Source.
  - (b) Offer to publish the Source to the same groups.
  - (c) Keep today's check and document it.
- **Code today**
  - Roam warns only when the Source isn't in this space's database at all. It never checks the target group.
  - With suggestive mode on, every node syncs, so the warning never shows. With it off, the warning stops once the Source has been published to any group. An imported Source never warns.
  - Obsidian runs the same existence check and writes only to the console.
  - The destination then shows the placeholder and says "Import the source, then refresh this page", which the user can't do because the Source isn't shared with them.
- **Recommended default:** (a). It's the smallest change that explains the placeholder the destination ends up with. Expected result: publish warns, in both suggestive modes, that the target group can't see the Source.

## DSC-06: When a space leaves a group, do its shared nodes stay visible and keep updating for the group?

- **Options**
  - (a) Yes. Leaving doesn't unshare anything (today).
  - (b) Nodes stay visible but stop updating.
  - (c) Leaving removes the space's grants to that group.
- **Code today**
  - Grants belong to the group. Leaving (website only) deletes the membership row and nothing else, so the group keeps seeing the nodes, and the source keeps syncing updates to them.
  - No app removes a space's access to a group.
- **Recommended default:** (a) for v0, documented, to stay consistent with "no unshare in v0" (PUB-04 and DEL-03). Expected result: after A leaves G, G's members still see N and its updates, and A no longer sees G's other nodes.

## TXT-04: May an imported Obsidian note's links and tags become page references in Roam?

- **Options**
  - (a) Keep `[[link]]` and `#tag` as Roam page references (today), and accept that Roam may create pages for them.
  - (b) As (a), but translate `[[Other|alias]]` into Roam's alias form, `[alias]([[Other]])`.
  - (c) Turn links whose target isn't in the graph into plain text.
- **Code today**
  - Links and tags reach Roam's markdown import unchanged, so Roam parses them as page references. Whether Roam then creates empty pages is Roam's own behavior; the case observes it.
  - `[[Other|alias]]` isn't translated, so it references a page literally named "Other|alias".
  - A linked file that is also embedded in the note is rewritten to the copied asset.
- **Recommended default:** (b). References match how Roam users write and keep the links navigable. The alias form is the one construct that produces a wrong page name. Expected result: `[[Some note]]` and `#tag` are page references, and `[[Other|alias]]` shows "alias" linked to "Other".

## TXT-06: Must Refresh keep block ids and local additions on an imported Roam page?

- **Options**
  - (a) No. Refresh replaces the page content (today). Document imported pages as copies that Refresh overwrites.
  - (b) Keep block ids where the text is unchanged.
  - (c) Keep local child blocks in a marked section that Refresh leaves alone.
- **Code today**
  - Refresh adds the new content, then deletes every old block with its children. The page uid survives. Block uids don't, so block references into the page break and local additions are deleted.
  - The title's Refresh button always forces, so each click rewrites the page even when nothing changed. Refresh-all skips unchanged pages.
- **Recommended default:** (a) for v0. UC5 says Refresh overwrites without duplicates, which this does. (b) and (c) are post-v0. Expected result: after Refresh, the page holds the source content only; references into the old blocks no longer resolve.

## TTL-11: Two nodes from two spaces decorate to the same Roam title. What happens to the second import?

- **Options**
  - (a) Refuse it (today), with a message that names the other page's source space.
  - (b) Import it under a disambiguated title, for example with the source space name appended.
  - (c) Offer to link the second node to the existing page.
- **Code today**
  - When both map to the same local type, both become "[[CLM]] - Sleep helps", and the second import fails: "A page titled … already exists and was not imported from "<raw RID>". Rename or remove that page, then import again". The raw RID is shown.
  - The import list's Source space column does tell the two apart.
  - Renaming the first page lets the second import, but the first page's next Refresh then fails trying to rename it back.
- **Recommended default:** (a) for v0, with the message naming the space instead of the raw RID. Document that one graph holds only one of two same-titled nodes; (b) is the follow-up. Expected result: the second import fails with a message naming the page and its source space, and nothing is overwritten.

## TTL-15: A shared Roam node is renamed so no node type matches. What should happen?

- **Options**
  - (a) Treat it as unshared: remove it from the database like a deleted node.
  - (b) Keep sharing the last synced version (today) and tell the author it no longer updates.
  - (c) Keep syncing it under its last known type.
- **Code today**
  - Sync skips it with no message (an analytics event only). Cleanup removes only pages that no longer exist, so the last version stays shared, and destinations can still import and refresh it.
  - The publish dialog no longer lists it. Renaming it back resumes updates.
- **Recommended default:** (b), as a known gap in v0 without the notice. (a) would drop the node's grants on a typo, and renaming back wouldn't restore them. Expected result: the last version stays shared and importable, and renaming back resumes updates.

## AST-06: Should files that an Obsidian note links to, without embedding, travel with it?

- **Options**
  - (a) Embeds only (today). Document that linked files arrive as dead links.
  - (b) Upload every linked vault file too.
  - (c) Upload linked files that aren't notes (PDFs, images, documents), the same way as embeds.
- **Code today**
  - Only embedded files are uploaded.
  - A linked `[[doc.pdf]]` becomes a Roam page reference named "doc.pdf", or a dead link under `import/<space>/` in Obsidian.
  - When the same file is also embedded in the note, the link is rewritten to the copy.
- **Recommended default:** (c). A dead link is worse than no link, research notes often link PDFs this way, and the upload path already exists for embeds. Expected result: a linked PDF opens from the destination copy. If this is too much for v0, (a) with a documented known gap is the fallback.

## AST-08: Where should imported assets land in an Obsidian vault?

- **Options**
  - (a) Today's rule, kept for v0.
  - (b) Always `import/<space>/<full source path>`.
  - (c) One attachments folder per space, or the vault's configured attachment folder.
- **Code today**
  - Assets go under `import/<space>/`. The path below that is relative to the source note's folder when the asset sits inside that folder; otherwise it is the asset's full source vault path.
  - An asset already imported with the same hash reuses its existing path. A name that sanitizes to nothing becomes `asset-<hash8>`. The space folder gets a short suffix on a name clash.
- **Recommended default:** (a). It's implemented, the last bug bash only asked the question, and no case shows harm. Revisit if testers can't find assets. Expected result: the case records the rule above, and every embed in the imported note resolves.

## UPD-09: Should a destination show that a newer version of an imported node exists?

- **Options**
  - (a) No indicator in v0 (today). Users refresh a node or run refresh-all.
  - (b) A "changed at source" marker on the imported page or note.
  - (c) List imported nodes that have updates in the import dialog, with an Update action.
- **Code today**
  - Both import lists hide nodes that are already imported, and neither app compares times.
  - Updates come only from the Refresh button on the imported page or note, and from the refresh-all commands ("DG: Refresh all imported nodes"; "Fetch latest content from imported nodes").
- **Recommended default:** (a) for v0, documented. Refresh-all is the update path, so its counts have to be right first (UPD-04). Expected result: no indicator; refresh-all brings the change.

## REL-05: Should a relation the user removed at the destination stay removed?

- **Options**
  - (a) Yes. Remember the dismissed relation and skip it on later imports.
  - (b) No. It comes back as pending (today); document it.
- **Code today**
  - Roam's "Remove relation" deletes the block and records nothing. The next dialog import of any node, from any space, re-creates it as pending. A deleted accepted relation comes back as pending too.
  - In Obsidian, pending relations have only an Accept button; only accepted ones can be deleted. The next Refresh, "Fetch latest content from imported nodes" or import from that space re-adds a deleted one as pending.
- **Recommended default:** (a). If a rejected relation returns after every import, reviewing it is pointless. Obsidian also needs a reject action on pending relations. Expected result: a removed relation doesn't return on later imports or refreshes.

## REL-07 and REL-08: When does a relation added after both nodes were shared reach a destination that already has both?

- **Options**
  - (a) Match Obsidian in both roles. A Roam source shares the relation at its next sync when both endpoints are shared to the same group. A Roam destination imports relations for the node it refreshes.
  - (b) Keep Roam as it is: the relation is shared only when an endpoint is published again, and it arrives only with a dialog import.
- **Code today**
  - Roam source: sync has no relation step, so a new relation is shared only when an endpoint is published again from the publish dialog.
  - Obsidian source: a relation is shared when it's created, for groups both endpoints are published to, and every full sync reconciles relation grants.
  - Roam destination: Refresh never imports relations. They arrive only with a dialog import, and that needs a node selected to import.
  - Obsidian destination: Refresh imports relations for the whole source space.
- **Recommended default:** (a). Obsidian is the reference flow and already does this. Expected result: after the source's next sync, a Refresh of either endpoint at the destination shows the new relation as pending.

## REL-09: The source deletes a relation that a destination has pending or accepted. What happens there?

- **Options**
  - (a) Remove pending copies at the next import or Refresh; keep accepted ones as the destination's own.
  - (b) Remove both.
  - (c) Keep both (today) and document it.
- **Code today**
  - The source removes the relation from the database at cleanup (Obsidian at full sync, Roam every sync), and a trigger drops its grants.
  - Destinations only add or update relations, so pending and accepted copies both stay.
- **Recommended default:** (a). Pending means nobody has reviewed it, so an upstream deletion should withdraw it. Accepted means the destination chose it. Expected result: the pending copy disappears at the next import or Refresh; the accepted copy stays.

## SEC-03: Can any member of a group delete the group's grants for another space's node?

- **Options**
  - (a) Only editors of the node's own space can delete its grants.
  - (b) Group admins can too.
  - (c) Any member can (today).
- **Code today:** the grant delete rule allows editors of the node's space, or any member of the grantee group, admin or not. Members can also list those grants. Inserting and updating grants is editor-only.
- **Recommended default:** (a). Removing a grant unshares another space's node for everyone in the group, which is the owner's call, and it matches the insert rule. Expected result: a non-editor member's delete is refused.

## SEC-04: Does removing a group's space access also end reads through that group's existing per-node grants?

- **Options**
  - (a) Yes. Table and storage reads require the same space access the views do.
  - (b) No. Per-node grants stand alone; space access only affects the views.
  - (c) Removing space access also deletes the group's grants for that space.
- **Code today**
  - The views need space access plus a grant. The table read rules (Concept, Content, Document, FileReference) and storage access accept a grant alone, and nothing deletes grants when space access is removed.
  - No app removes space access; only an editor of the space can. Some app paths read the tables directly, for example Obsidian's refresh reads Content, so they would still get rows.
- **Recommended default:** (a). Every reader then agrees with the views, and the grants survive if access is restored. Expected result: after removal, nothing of A's is readable by G's members through the views, the tables or storage. The explicit grant-removal control also ends reads.

## Not covered here

- Settled by the review: SRC-03 (the placeholder was chosen; the collision fallback is SRC-12) and TXT-08 (the heading-removal premise no longer holds).
- Decide cases at P2: DSC-09, TTL-07, SCH-06, UX-09.
- UX-06 (P2, high risk) also leaves one question open: whether the Obsidian import notice counts the Source that came along automatically.
